models.observations: Striped cloth roofs flank the axial path in front of the reed shop. Gold trade seal, open baskets, and bright vegetables read at phone size. Reviewed the serialized three-LOD chain [992, 510, 213] and full/64 px previews.

Opposing striped awnings, goods counters and a sun trade disk stay distinct under all three stepped shop roofs. Thin posts line up with their canopy corners. Reviewed the serialized three-LOD chain [1008, 510, 213] and full/64 px previews.

Cyan awnings, coral stripes, and the glazed stepped roof read as one future market. Vegetables and the small trade seal provide recognizable scale. Reviewed the serialized three-LOD chain [1018, 520, 223] and full/64 px previews.

The brick monitor sits above the two striped bays. Goods, center seal, and side pot stay clear against the darker Industrial base and lighter Modern row. Reviewed the serialized three-LOD chain [1058, 560, 235] and full/64 px previews.

The parked airframe has matching swept outer panels in the Information and Ascension views. The inward wingtip has daylight to the terminal at its own height, the outer wing stays on the apron, and the control lantern still anchors the airport silhouette. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 796/482/239.

The entrance stair meets the front of the beveled podium without the former LOD2 surface pair. The sail sign, deep teal portico and corner merchant's jar remain clear under both the Medieval green and Renaissance russet roof. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 750/427/147.

The shortened stair ends at the podium at all three levels. A sheltered doorway is clearly visible between its piers, and the double pennant and glazed charter room retain the guild identity in both rows. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 758/435/155.

The stair now meets the podium at its edge. The chimney and raised monitor roof keep a strong profile above the trade pennant as the Industrial brick shifts to the subdued Modern palette. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 868/521/201.

The freight stair runs directly up to the timber jetty, with the top tread outside the freight-deck surface. Sail, slung cargo and stout piles read together across all three age rows, including the darker Medieval roof. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 973/510/237.

The new landing terminates flush at the freight deck. White pier, cabin boat and crane remain separated by the blue water at thumbnail size, and the gilt trim gives the Ascension vessel a distinct finish. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 1051/588/255.

The collar between approach and pier is clean at all three LODs. The raised dock still has visible support posts, and the crane reaches the gunwale beside the small cargo boat in both the brick and pale gray variants. No exposed pairs reported in the serialized LODs 1029/566/255.

Against 91863de, the revised LOD1 changes 0.07% of front-view pixels and 0.15% of reverse-view pixels at 64 px (channel difference above 10).

models.observations: The train retains a continuous body beside the platform. The broad glazed canopy keeps its rim, two supporting posts and little boarding stair in the middle view.
The low locomotive and its wheels remain grounded on the track beside the brick station. The long green roof and rear enclosure retain their full silhouettes.

models.observations: The two chambers and elevated link form a sound structure. Their cylindrical walls and blue caps are easily confused with the GoldMine tanks. Both front doors are too small to establish the public meeting function. Painted previews cover information, ascension. I compared both 64 px unpainted family views and the 215°, 125° and 35° painted middle LOD. Serialized LODs 868/454/210 passed validation and the 60% ceiling. Direct surface and winding checks found zero exposed coplanar overlaps and zero inverted closed shells. The largest directed corner share involving this model and any sibling was 3.143%.
defects: Give the hall a public council entrance, gathering terrace or conspicuous charter standard that changes the two-chamber outline.

models.observations: The broad stair leads to a public colonnade beside a conspicuous charter banner. The folded turquoise roof stretches over the full assembly porch and changes its outline from both angles. At LOD1 the council hall retains its entry, stairs, charter and glazed enclosure. Painted previews cover information, ascension. I compared both 64 px unpainted family views and the 215°, 125° and 35° painted middle LOD. Serialized LODs 675/369/209 passed validation and the 60% ceiling. Direct surface and winding checks found zero exposed coplanar overlaps and zero inverted closed shells. The largest directed corner share involving this model and any sibling was 3.259%.

The tall annulus clears the squat Industrial bank in both 64 px unpainted views. The drum sits convincingly on its inclined podium. The teal stripe, inner gold lip and coin relief make an attractive facade, but the opening still dominates from front and back at all three LODs. On painted family page 02 the Ascension bank and Neutral AscensionGate both present a turquoise-and-gold hoop over an ivory plinth with centered stairs. The two authored previews shift the lining from steel to gold without resolving the duplicate landmark. Serialized LODs 1380/822/392 passed check_entry. Direct checks found zero exposed coplanar overlaps and zero inverted closed shells.
defects: At 64 px the open hoop reads as the AscensionGate before the lower coin door can identify the bank. Replace the open portal mass with a visibly enclosed treasury or strongroom and retain the Saurian stepped architecture and clear coin or vault front.

models.observations: At 64 px the glazed teller hall steps down from a solid, canted strongroom. Its hinge and concentric locking door stand proud of the wall, and the roof has two raised bands visible from the reverse. The Industrial bank has a centered rooftop crest and square tiers. The revised bank has a low asymmetrical outline in both unpainted views. On family page 02, the AscensionGate retains its tall open center while the bank reads as an enclosed treasury. The bronze coin-sized lock, gold hardware, narrow turquoise fascia and pale stepped base tie the taller vault to the public hall. The Information door has a steel rim and the Ascension door has a gold rim. LOD1 retains the door relief, hinges and roof bands. LOD2 retains the inset entrance, vault face and two building heights. All three serialized LODs passed check_entry at 1245/709/393 triangles. Direct surface and winding checks found zero exposed coplanar pairs and zero inverted closed shells. The revised vault shares zero rounded LOD0 corners in either direction with either older Saurian bank.
